look_here_first: Look for the true scarlet leatherflower: a nodding ovoid-to-urn-shaped flower with thick rose-red to scarlet sepals and sharply recurved tips, but without the expanded crispate margins of C. pitcheri.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — TPWD rare-species list/preserve reports; Bandera — TPWD plus Lost Maples field records; Real — TPWD/field-survey element occurrence material.

best_field_traits: 1-pinnate leaves with 6–10 leaflets plus tendril-like terminal leaflet
four thick scarlet sepals with non-expanded non-crispate margins
morphology_keys.habit: Perennial climbing vine to roughly 3 m.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: 1-pinnate; 6–10 leathery leaflets plus a tendril-like terminal leaflet; often glaucous beneath and reticulate.
morphology_keys.flower: Axillary scarlet leathery urn; sepal margins not expanded or crispate; tips recurved.
morphology_keys.joey_field_observation: Joey Santore's West Texas native-plant landscaping video includes an exact Clematis texensis frame showing vine habit and leaf context.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. pitcheri is usually purple and has expanded crispate distal sepal margins with shorter weakly hairy achene beaks. C. drummondii has open white flowers and extremely long plumose fruit tails.

photo_note: Public-domain wild Bandera images recorded; Joey vine frame retained as private-study source context.
